{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Ronald Alan Fintushel''' (born 1945) is an American mathematician, specializing in low-dimensional [[geometric topology]] (specifically of 4-[[manifold]]s) and the mathematics of [[gauge theory]].

==Education and career==
Fintushel studied mathematics at [[Columbia University]] with a bachelor's degree in 1967 and at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] with a master's degree in 1969.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ronald Fintushel, University Distinguished Professor of Mathematics, Emeritus|website=Michigan State University|url=https://users.math.msu.edu/users/ronfint/}}</ref> In 1975 he received his Ph.D. from the [[State University of New York at Binghamton]] with thesis ''Orbit maps of local <math>S^1</math>-actions on manifolds of dimension less than five '' under the supervision of Louis McAuley.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=15589}}</ref> Fintushel was a professor at [[Tulane University]] and is a professor at [[Michigan State University]].

His research deals with geometric topology, in particular of 4-manifolds (including the computation of Donaldson and Seiberg-Witten invariants) with links to gauge theory, [[knot theory]], and [[symplectic geometry]]. He works closely with [[Ronald J. Stern]].

In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker, with Ronald J. Stern, with talk ''Construction of smooth 4-manifolds'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Fintushel, Ronald|author2=Stern, Ronald J.|chapter=Construction of smooth 4-manifolds|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=443–452|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011700000}}</ref> In 1997 Fintushel received the Distinguished Faculty Award from Michigan State University. In 2016 a conference was held in his honor at Tulane University.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.faculty.virginia.edu/tmark/FintushelConf/|title=Topology of 4-Manifolds: A Conference in Honor of the First Anniversary of Ronald Fintushel's 60th Birthday, November 10–12, 2006, Tulane University}}</ref>

He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. Fintushel is a member of the editorial boards of ''[[Geometry & Topology]]'' and the ''[[Michigan Mathematical Journal]]''.

==Selected publications==
*with Stern: ''Constructing lens spaces by surgery on knots'', Mathematische Zeitschrift, vol. 175, 1980, pp.&nbsp;33–51 
*with Stern: ''An exotic free involution of <math>S^4</math>'', Annals of Mathematics, vol. 113, 1981, pp.&nbsp;357–365
*with Stern: [https://faculty.sites.uci.edu/rstern/files/2011/03/23_PseudoFreeOrbifolds.pdf ''Pseudofree orbifolds''], Annals of Mathematics, vol. 122, 1985, pp.&nbsp;335–364
*with Stern: [https://faculty.sites.uci.edu/rstern/files/2011/03/28_Inst_Homology.pdf ''Instanton homology of Seifert fibred homology three spheres''], Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, vol. 61, 1990, pp.&nbsp;109–137
*with Stern: ''Immersed spheres in 4-manifolds and the immersed Thom conjecture'', Turkish Journal of Mathematics, vol. 19, 1995, pp.&nbsp;145–157
*with Stern: ''Donaldson invariants of 4-manifolds with simple type'', J. Diff. Geom., vol. 42, 1995, pp.&nbsp;577–633
*with Stern: ''The blowup formula for Donaldson invariants'', Annals of Mathematics, vol.  143, 1996, pp.&nbsp;529–546 [https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9405002 arXiv]
*with Stern: ''Rational blowdowns of smooth 4-manifolds'', Journal of Differential Geometry, vol. 46, 1997, pp.&nbsp;181–235 [https://arxiv.org/abs/alg-geom/9505018 arXiv]
*with Stern: ''Surfaces in 4-manifolds'', Math. Res. Letters, vol. 4, 1997, pp.&nbsp;907–914 [https://arxiv.org/abs/dg-ga/9705009 arXiv]
*with Stern: ''Knots, links, and 4-manifolds'', Inventiones mathematicae, vol. 134, 1998, pp.&nbsp;363–400, [https://arxiv.org/abs/dg-ga/9612014 arXiv]
*with Stern: [http://faculty.sites.uci.edu/rstern/files/2011/03/45_ICM-copy.pdf ''Constructions of smooth 4-manifolds.''] Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. II (Berlin, 1998). Doc. Math. 1998, Extra Vol. II, 443–452
*with Stern: ''Symplectic surfaces in a fixed homology class'', J. Diff. Geom., vol. 52, 2000, pp.&nbsp;203–222
*with Stern: ''Families of simply connected 4-manifolds with the same Seiberg-Witten invariants'', Topology, vol. 43, 2004, pp.&nbsp;1449–1467	
*with Stern: ''Invariants for Lagrangian tori'', Geom. Topol., vol. 8, 2004, pp., 947-968 [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304402 arXiv]
*with Stern: [https://msp.org/gtm/2004/07/gtm-2004-07-013s.pdf Tori in symplectic 4-manifolds], Geometry and Topology Monographs, vol. 7, 2004, Proceedings of the Casson Fest, pp.&nbsp;311–333
*with Stern, B. D. Park: ''Reverse engineering small 4-manifolds'', Algebraic & Geometric Topology, vol. 7, 2007, pp.&nbsp;2103–2116 [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701846 arXiv]
*with Stern: ''Six Lectures on Four 4-manifolds'', Low dimensional topology, IAS/Park City Math. Ser. 15, Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI, 2009, pp.&nbsp;265–315
